messages:
alice.nguyen: FYI I'm seeing a spike in 503s on /v1/generate for us-west-2. latency > 10s for a lot of requests. could be the batcher. paging alerts firing too.
ben.shah: grabbing logs, looks like multiple runtime pods restarted on node gpu-node-17 around the same time. kube shows node flapping.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — Sev2 — continuous-batcher node flapping causing customer errors. Incident lead: @carla.lewis. Pager duty: @dinesh.patel.
carla.lewis: I'm on it. @dinesh can you triage node health while I look at batcher telem? customer impact: some production customers seeing timeouts and errors.
dinesh.patel: running `kubectl get nodes gpu-node-17 -o wide` now. node reports NotReady, kubelet restarting frequently. dmesg shows repeated GPU driver oops: "NVRM: Xid (0x1e)" and then GPU reset.
eva.morales: that explains CUDA errors in runtime logs: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` followed by container restart. also seeing batcher queue length trending up — requests piling into the continuous-batcher process.
alice.nguyen: stack traces from batcher show it's not releasing requests when the GPU fails: we accumulate prefixes in the in-memory queue until OOM.
ben.shah: low-level logs:```
I0328 14:01:12 batcher.go:412] enqueue request id=abcd
I0328 14:01:12 batcher.go:540] batch size now 512 (cap 64) // bug: cap ignored on surge
E0328 14:01:14 runtime.cu:274] cuda: lost device, Xid 0x1e
E0328 14:01:14 batcher.go:616] failed dispatch: device unavailable
panic: runtime out of memory
```
carla.lewis: ok, two failure modes: 1) GPU driver crash causes device resets -> runtime containers crash. 2) batcher doesn't handle transient device-unavailable errors and keeps growing batches (the cap was ignored), hitting memory OOMs and taking pods down.
dinesh.patel: immediate mitigations: 1) cordon + drain gpu-node-17 to stop new pods landing there, 2) scale up batcher replicas to spread backlog (temporarily), 3) set a runtime config kill-switch to enforce batch_size_cap=64 and reject new queued requests above queue_limit.
alice.nguyen: adding short term ingress throttle to give us breathing room — rate-limit the affected route for hosted tier to 20rps. can we change that in the gateway?
deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered: patch-ingress-throttle -> rolling update of api-gateway (canary 5%).
eva.morales: I'm applying a runtime overlay to force batch_size_cap at the pod level: `kubectl set env deploy/continuous-batcher BATCH_MAX=64 --overwrite` on the canary first. will monitor.
ben.shah: while that's rolling, I'm going to cordon node and drain:```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
dinesh.patel: node drained. scheduling moved pods to gpu-node-22 and gpu-node-24. those nodes have older driver but stable.
carla.lewis: customers: Support ops — prepare a message for affected customers, include mitigation steps and ETA. we think degradation window ~ 15-45m depending on backlog.
support-ops: drafting now. will include note about intermittent 5xx and higher latencies; apologize and share workaround (retry after 10s).
alice.nguyen: After forcing BATCH_MAX=64 we saw batcher queue length drop from 120k -> 8k in 10m, and memory usage stabilized. good sign.
eva.morales: runtime pods on drained node kept restarting due to repeated Xid errors. we've flagged the NVIDIA driver version; suspect regression in 525 series. ops: recommend marking gpu-node-17 out for driver upgrade/rollback.
dinesh.patel: action items: 1) cordon gpu-node-17 (done), 2) blacklist driver version 525.89 on autoscaler, 3) create node pool with validated driver and cordon older nodes.
carla.lewis: decision: rollback continuous-batcher change from yesterday that introduced the batch cap bug in the policy layer. roll back to 2026-03-14 build (stable) after quick validation.
deploy-bot: Rollback triggered: continuous-batcher -> 2026-03-14-stable. Canary at 10% now.
ben.shah: canary looks healthy, batch size enforcement present, no surge to >64. will promote in 5.
alice.nguyen: monitoring: 5xx rate down from 4.2% -> 0.6% in 20m, p95 latency back to ~120ms.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED — mitigation applied, partial recovery observed. still monitoring for node-level driver regressions.
carla.lewis: timeline summary for postmortem: 14:00 UTC — GPU driver Xid spikes on gpu-node-17 -> node flapped. 14:02 — runtime pods errored and restarted. 14:03 — continuous-batcher ignored queue cap, batches grew uncontrollably and caused OOMs. 14:05 — alerts fired. 14:08 — cordon+drain applied, ingress throttled, batch cap forced. 14:27 — rollback deployed. 14:45 — metrics normalized.
support-ops: customer notification sent at 14:35 UTC.
eva.morales: follow-ups: - Add backlog circuit-breaker to batcher (reject beyond N requests) - Harden device-failure handling so batcher can quickly fail and requeue to other nodes - Add driver-version gating on node autoscaler - Add a metric for batcher queue growth anomaly and an alert threshold
dinesh.patel: I'll own the driver gating and node pool work. alice you take backlog circuit-breaker?
alice.nguyen: yes I'll take the circuit-breaker and a quick PoC by EOD.
carla.lewis: assigning postmortem owners and timeline. great job on quick mitigation. reactions: :tada: :heart: :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — root cause mitigation applied, long-term actions scheduled.
